scope.publication: Informal research notebook; not peer reviewed. Selected saved evidence, not a full model or dataset release.
scope.method: Consolidated project documentation and selected saved results. No training, inference, historical test suite or GPU benchmark was rerun during publication.

synthesis.headline: Working mechanisms, real storage gains, and one promising steering pilot
synthesis.intro: The portfolio now spans original sphere models, shared fields, compression and runtime studies, coding agents, four nested-core revisions, and eight pretrained 7B revisions. Its strongest repeatable lessons concern what geometry changes, where storage or memory can be reduced, and which simple controls explain the gains. Useful learned steering has a positive single-seed result in nested-core v4, while broader language-model and coding advantages remain unestablished.

findings.label: Mechanism
findings.title: Routes change computation; changed computation is not automatically better
findings.text: The original sphere learned task-dependent expert paths, and activation interventions in later routing studies changed subsequent group or neuron selections. V6 of the pretrained 7B line went further: coordinates selected actual MLP nodes, with coordinate changes altering logits. These are substantive implementation results. Across the original scaling, routing and steering studies, however, simpler straight, fixed, ordinary-routing or compact residual controls usually matched or exceeded measured quality or efficiency.

findings.label: Storage
findings.title: Compact representations work when their assumptions fit the task
findings.text: Shared fields reduced storage on structured handwriting and known-association tasks, but larger recall sets and corruptions exposed capacity and robustness tradeoffs. Post-training compression produced practical artifacts: Granite's six-bit model passed limited quality screens at 22.245 GiB, and a later validation-selected mixed-precision artifact passed its fresh screen at 16.464 GiB. Uniform six-bit, fixed four-bit and random mixed controls also remain important evidence. The gains come from sharing, quantization and compact replacements; they do not establish exceptional knowledge density from curvature alone.

findings.label: Runtime
findings.title: Measure complete execution; fewer operations or less VRAM can cost more time
findings.text: CPU/GPU splits and sparse routes were functionally correct, but dependent transfers and dispatch frequently outweighed arithmetic savings. The small CPU-actor/GPU-learner PPO experiment is a positive exception. Offloading in pretrained 7B v3 greatly reduced GPU allocation while sharply increasing latency. V7 substantially improved the earlier route executor, yet learned routes still cost more than its fixed and dense controls. Storage, peak tensors, actual latency and parameter-application counts should remain separate measures.

findings.label: From scratch
findings.title: Bounded internal memory did not establish a working coding agent
findings.text: The small and 7.35B MemorySphere projects demonstrated custom full-stack training, fixed scratch-state memory and checkpoint integrity. Their task results remained weak. The later 7.41B ten-hour run finished 22,042 updates and 4.77 million supervised tokens, improving token losses but producing no successful coding workflows. Final scoring was time-limited: 0/60 tasks at eight visits and 0/40 with adaptive stopping, from two requested 96-task panels. The later check-in found invalid tool actions throughout those recorded panels.

findings.label: Positive pilot
findings.title: Preserving input information made steering useful in nested-core v4
findings.text: The nested-core sequence progressed from shared-slice feasibility to a fixed whole core, larger cores, and an input-preserving skip. In v4's seed-7 experiment, 512 answer-prefix cases came from 32 program files. Enabling redirects increased the same shared checkpoint's accuracy from 52.73% to 57.62%; the separately trained clean model reached 57.03%. The 4.89-point increase is against disabled redirects, not the clean baseline. NLL comparisons had positive paired-program intervals. Both clean and shared models benefited from the representation change. This is a local replication lead, limited by one seed, reused holdouts, near-chance longer-program core reasoning and higher latency than clean inference.

findings.label: Pretrained 7B
findings.title: Learned 7B control still needs to beat fixed and shuffled routes
findings.text: The pretrained Mistral line verified exact shared storage, bounded update scope and progressively richer routing. V7's stage policy did not outperform fixed or shuffled controls; its arbitrary recurrent pilot lost answer quality, and the latest RL continuation remained at 50% with a constant answer and path after 512 total updates. V8 produced diverse actions and a small test-point advantage, but intervals and shuffled controls did not establish input-specific benefit. Its frozen release rule therefore keeps fixed (2,2) as the application default. V8 branches from stage-ordered v7, not its later RL continuation.

findings.label: Coding
findings.title: Extra visits and controller RL have not yielded dependable coding gains
findings.text: Think's recurrent small model did not approach its 14B capability reference; Revisit's compute-matched routing comparison did not beat ordinary recurrence. LongHorizon's compact pre-RL variant solved one additional task in its four-task pilot, but the difference depended on an output cap, and controller RL regressed both that result and cumulative workflow behavior. These studies support preserving trained zero-step, ordinary recurrence and pre-RL controls, while scoring complete tool workflows rather than attractive routes or isolated token-loss improvements.

findings.label: Evidence
findings.title: The archive is rich, but its experiments are not one combined benchmark
findings.text: Saved protocols, per-example outcomes, audits and source/checkpoint identities make the work reviewable. Comparisons still span different tasks, denominators, seeds, model sizes, training budgets, precision formats and execution paths. Several later revisions are adaptive pilots; program-bootstrap intervals do not represent seed uncertainty. Untrained stress tests establish execution only. This consolidation indexes saved evidence and reported verification; it does not rerun model inference, tests, training or GPU benchmarks, and it does not infer live process state from old status files.

priorities: Replicate nested-core v4 with additional seeds and a newly sequestered program holdout. Keep input-preserving clean/shared arms, zero-turn and one-turn controls, and record later-decision utility as well as total accuracy.

For pretrained 7B routing, require gains over validation-selected fixed and shuffled policies before enabling learned control by default. Treat stage routing, arbitrary recurrence and RL continuation as distinct experiments.

For from-scratch coding, diagnose valid tool generation and cached/full-context behavior before extending training. Complete the fixed held-out panels and report code correctness, valid edits and finished workflows separately from token loss.

Choose a practical storage or runtime target, then compare complete artifacts and full request cost under matched quality and runtime conditions. Preserve simpler quantizers, compact residuals, CPU-only execution and dense/fixed routes as controls.

reconciliations.title: The 7.41B training run is complete, not still underway
reconciliations.text: The earlier live-run description is superseded by COMPLETE.json and the November 24 check-in: ten hours and 22,042 updates finished. Training completion must remain separate from the incomplete final evaluation and absence of demonstrated coding success.

reconciliations.title: The overview must include later nested-core and pretrained 7B work
reconciliations.text: The original handoff predates much of the nested-core and pretrained 7B progression. This index adds those branches, including v4's positive exploratory steering result, v7's recurrent/RL work and continuation, and v8's fixed-policy release decision. A blanket claim that every steering experiment failed would omit the v4 result.

reconciliations.title: Granite's top-level results are not its last compression result
reconciliations.text: The six-bit and single-block reports are followed by rl_compression, which produced a 16.464 GiB validation-selected artifact and a fresh final quality screen. Its data subset differs from the earlier report, and its RL policy assigns precision offline rather than controlling reasoning during inference.

reconciliations.title: Use the deployed v6 scores where cached-tree metrics differ
reconciliations.text: The saved deployed verification supersedes cached-tree numerical outcomes. Matching route actions did not guarantee identical logits or all predictions; the consolidation uses the deployed-path comparison and preserves the mismatch as a limitation.

reconciliations.title: V7's latest RL snapshot and v8's ancestry are different branches
reconciliations.text: The latest saved v7 RL evidence is the continuation at 512 cumulative updates, still showing constant-answer chance performance. V8 inherits the stage-ordered branch and releases fixed (2,2); it should not be described as a successful continuation of the RL-trained recurrent model.

projects.name: Original sphere and scaling studies
projects.purpose: Test whether input-dependent cubic Bezier routes through a sphere can select useful expert computation, then measure accuracy, storage, speed and robustness against simpler controls.
work: Implemented learned surface entry/exit, interior control points, sparse top-k expert dispatch, a carried feature vector and a trained decoder; added a scalar Bezier-transfer variant.
Trained five digit-classification architectures across three seeds on a fixed 1,078/359/360 split; saved checkpoints, route interventions, CPU/GPU verification and an offline viewer.
Completed 92 scaling runs using EMNIST, up to 100,000 training images, and synthetic association recall up to 16,384 facts; compared routed, full-residual and compact-residual models.
Benchmarked 15 untrained execution configurations up to 68.1 million parameters; derived and numerically checked routing factorization, structured weight sharing and restricted commuting dynamics.
Published architecture, reproduction and methodology documents plus shared activation and recurrent-computation visualizations.

findings.text: Original digits: Bezier routing achieved 96.76% mean accuracy across seeds 7, 19 and 42, versus 96.67% for residual and 97.13% for straight routing. Bezier batch-one latency was 0.992 ms versus 0.471 ms residual; no general accuracy or speed advantage was established.

Routes affect computation: shuffling routes lowered mean digit accuracy from 96.76% to 88.52%, bypassing interior transformations to 64.91%, and straightening trained curves to 96.30%. These are interventions on trained models, not retrained controls.

At the largest trained EMNIST setting, Bezier used 8.900 MiB at 83.59% accuracy and 1.234 ms batch-one latency; compact residual used 2.830 MiB at 84.04% and 0.457 ms. Means cover two seeds and 18,800 test images.

At 16,384 synthetic associations, medium Bezier reached 99.98% fresh-query recall in 1.130 MiB; medium compact residual reached 100% in 0.605 MiB. Stronger-noise recall was 69.43% versus 61.06%, showing a task-specific tradeoff rather than a universal storage/reliability win.

The saved verification covers all 92 scaling checkpoints and passes source, data, partition, checkpoint and report-link checks. The original digit verification separately reloads all 15 checkpoints. These are recorded checks, not tests rerun for this index.

At 68.1M random-weight parameters, Bezier versus full residual latency was 0.969 versus 3.012 ms at batch one, but 5.767 versus 3.578 ms at batch 128. Accounted batch-128 memory was 775.78 versus 261.77 MiB. Sparse computation did not remove stored weights or dispatcher allocations.

Algebra checks gave routing-score rank four and 2.66e-15 reconstruction error. A deliberately cubic 64-matrix bank compressed 16x with near-zero error, while independent random matrices incurred 0.968 relative error. The 16x result is bank-only and depends on constructed structure.

limitations: Digit results use one fixed small split; scaling uses two seeds and one image domain. Synthetic known-key recall is not natural-language knowledge.
Timing is eager float32 on the recorded RTX 5090 with device-resident inputs; transfer, preprocessing, startup and loading are excluded.
The 68.1M execution sweep is untrained. Algebraic constructions do not establish real-world model compression or language-model quality.
Additional sampling steps change the implemented model; reversing a drawn route does not invert computation.
projects.status: Completed local proof of concept, trained scaling study, untrained execution sweep and algebra checks; no overall geometry advantage established.
next_steps: Recommendation: retain matched-accuracy compact residual and ordinary routing controls when evaluating a new geometric architecture.
Recommendation: improve dispatch before drawing broader throughput conclusions, then test additional tasks and seeds.
projects.date_note: Source reports and algebra checks dated November 23, 2026; indexed November 25, 2026.

projects.name: Bezier-Routing
projects.purpose: Test whether intermediate neural activations can redirect later Bezier routes, groups, and individual neurons.
work: Implemented individual-neuron, group, and hierarchical routing with matched entry-state controls, straight routes, and direct selection.
Completed 24 training runs on the reused digits split; saved checkpoints, prediction traces, intervention paths, and geometry/reload verification.

findings.text: Perturbing two activation components after hop 1 changed 44.80% of later neuron-selection sets and 16.35% of later group sets in the feedback hierarchy; the frozen hierarchy changed neither. Feedback is causally active.

Digit accuracy with versus without feedback was 95.37% versus 94.54% for individual neurons, 96.85% versus 95.93% for groups, and 94.35% versus 95.19% for the hierarchy. All paired-image 95% intervals include zero.

The trained feedback hierarchy fell from 94.35% to 89.54% when feedback was disabled and to 50.19% when neuron updates were bypassed. Reliance on a mechanism does not establish superiority to a separately trained control.
All 24 saved checkpoints reproduced predictions and passed intervention/geometry checks; 13 unit checks were reported passed.

limitations: Only three seeds and 360 reused held-out digit images; exploratory accuracy intervals exclude training-seed uncertainty.
Group-only executes 96 neuron calls versus 24 for individual/hierarchical modes; no clean latency advantage is claimed.
projects.status: Completed mechanism study; feedback works, general quality gain unestablished.
next_steps: Recommendation: Test fresh tasks with matched budgets and training-seed uncertainty before extending accuracy claims.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Explore
projects.purpose: Determine whether shared smooth processing fields and analytic integration can reduce storage and execution cost.
work: Completed a 72-run main study and 18-run second-width recall study, covering handwriting, known-key associations, and synthetic smooth conditional transforms.
Implemented shared nonlinear fields, commuting linear analytic fields, straight/constant/direct gates, and residual controls.

findings.text: On handwriting, shared Bezier used 510.4 KiB versus 1475.9 KiB for the original expert model (2.89x smaller), at 83.90% versus 83.88% accuracy. Constant gates reached 83.91% with still less storage, favoring weight sharing over a curvature-specific explanation.

For 4,096 known random associations, shared Bezier achieved 100% recall at 6.05x less storage; straight, constant, direct-gate, and residual controls also reached 100%. At 16,384 associations the narrow shared model fell to 30.29%; width 256 reached 95.81% versus 99.988% for the original width-128 model.

On the synthetic interpolation gap, analytic Bezier had normalized MSE 0.000496 versus 0.014439 for the original and used 76.9 versus 1076.8 KiB. Analytic straight was better still at 0.000386. The analytic evaluator was 1.63-3.16x faster than the smallest tested RK4 setting meeting relative output error <=1e-5.

Robustness did not generally improve: stronger-noise recall was 74.48% versus 90.20% for 4,096 associations; noisy handwriting accuracy was 57.30% versus 61.72%. All 90 models reportedly reproduced saved test predictions.

limitations: Two seeds; width sweep only for the larger recall task; no large language-model evaluation.
Analytic integration requires commuting linear operators and polynomial rates; it is not a general nonlinear solver.
Capacity-run latency was affected by another workload; compact fields trade capacity for storage.
projects.status: Completed 90-checkpoint study; conditional storage and analytic-compute gains demonstrated.
next_steps: Recommendation: Prioritize structured shared-field tasks; run quality-matched capacity/training sweeps before claiming general knowledge compression.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Compress
projects.purpose: Compress pretrained SmolLM2 weights using cubic fits or curve-controlled codebooks while measuring language and QA preservation.
work: Completed 20 primary comparisons on 135M and 1.7B SmolLM2, plus a seven-case exploratory zero-anchored follow-up.

Compared direct/sorted cubic fitting, quantized curve/free codebooks, uniform int4/int8, and low-rank approximation; counted complete artifact bytes and independently reconstructed 22 distinct artifacts.

findings.text: Only ordinary int8 passed all prespecified validation/test preservation thresholds at both sizes. For 1.7B, int8 used 1779.56 MiB versus 3267.52 MiB FP16 and retained 99.46% of reference-correct answers.

Primary 1.7B cubic-codebook int4 used 1011.59 MiB (3.23x reduction), but perplexity rose from 10.706 to 16.200 and QA fell from 72.95% to 63.18%. Lower weight reconstruction error did not imply better model behavior.

On a separate follow-up subset, zero anchoring improved cubic-codebook perplexity from 16.551 to 12.271 and QA from 62.30% to 70.31%. It still missed preservation thresholds against FP16 (10.720 perplexity; 74.12% QA); a free zero-anchored codebook was similarly effective.

Saved completion checks record 27 evaluation cases, 22 reconstructed artifacts, and 23 passed unit tests. The tested runtime reconstructs dense FP16 weights and does not reduce steady-state GPU parameter memory.

limitations: One model family, two sizes, simple quantization baselines, no compression-aware training.
Follow-up is a fresh subset of the same corpora, not an independent dataset; zero anchoring and control precision changed together.
No compressed execution kernel or demonstrated inference-speed benefit.
projects.status: Completed primary and exploratory compression studies; ordinary int8 is the robust preservation result.
next_steps: Recommendation: Compare against stronger activation-aware quantizers and evaluate a packed runtime separately from artifact compression.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Granite
projects.purpose: Adapt a local Granite 4.2 30B checkpoint to a 32 GB GPU using six-bit packed weights and test a compact feedback-routed replacement block.
work: Built uniform6 and Bezier6 standalone artifacts, frozen language/QA screens, streamed BF16 reference evaluation, and a packed on-GPU runtime.
Distilled one layer-32 MLP into a compact shared field; compared curved, straight, frozen-feedback, and fixed controls; exported the replacement independently.

Completed a separate offline mixed-precision RL compression study: sixteen REINFORCE updates over 64 sampled section assignments, matched random search, fixed-bit controls, frozen validation selection, and a fresh final test.

findings.text: Six-bit artifacts occupy 22.245 GiB versus 54.532 GiB reference payload. On 16,384 WikiText-2 tokens and 256 ARC-Easy questions, Bezier6 had perplexity 20.0582, QA 82.03%, and 98.58% reference-correct retention, passing the project's screens. Uniform6 also passed.
Packed Bezier6 retained 22.235 GiB persistent tensors, with 23.567 GiB peak allocation; separately reconstructed dense last-token logits matched exactly. One 32-token prefill took 0.958 seconds.

The single-block standalone replacement used 21.960 GiB, saving 291.7 MiB versus the practical compressed artifact. All four fitted controls scored 81.25% QA; frozen feedback had the lowest replacement perplexity (20.2454 versus Bezier 20.2729). No added quality gain from curvature or feedback was established.

A latent perturbation changed 25.20% of later group choices in the Bezier replacement versus 0% for frozen feedback. This demonstrates adaptive routing, not better reasoning; local reconstruction relative MSE remained about 0.8021.

The later RL mixed-precision artifact used 16.464 GiB, 25.0% below the 21.960 GiB six-bit shared parent, and passed the prespecified validation and final quality screens. On the fresh 32768-token/512-question test it scored perplexity 18.2305, QA 80.86%, and original-correct retention 95.74%.

The RL policy chose 3/4/6-bit precision by four-layer section; it did not train inference-time reasoning. Fixed four-bit (15.429 GiB) and random mixed precision (15.636 GiB) also passed final test despite failing validation. RL had lower perplexity but occupied more storage; it did not establish dominance over these alternatives.

The mixed-precision artifact retained 16.454 GiB persistent GPU tensors and peaked at 17.790 GiB for the recorded inference/KV check. Packed versus reconstructed dense last-token logits matched exactly. Large same-artifact timing variation prevented a reliable generation-speed conclusion.

limitations: Limited quality screens and one block/fitting seed; no whole-model architectural conversion or broad reliability claim.
Eager current-matrix reconstruction targets residency, not fused low-bit speed; KV cache and driver/display memory are additional.
Reference size counts original tensor payload, while compressed size includes all artifact files.

The RL compression follow-up uses different fresh evaluation subsets from the earlier six-bit study; their perplexity and QA values must not be pooled. Its screen is point-estimate preservation, not statistical equivalence.
projects.status: Completed six-bit deployment, single-block adaptation, and later mixed-precision RL compression; smallest validation-selected screened artifact is 16.464 GiB.
next_steps: Recommendation: Retain uniform6 as a matched control; broaden tasks/context lengths and isolate replacement training from route geometry.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Engine
projects.purpose: Test CPU/GPU placements for the sphere model, including supervised learning, PPO, and GPU-produced curves evaluated on CPU.
work: Implemented CPU-only, GPU-only, GPU-matrix/CPU-activation, GPU-route/CPU-neuron, and CPU-actor/GPU-learner schedules.
Completed 54 inference configurations, 12 classifier and 15 PPO checkpoints; added pinned-buffer concurrent curve pipelines, tree workloads, and one-/four-layer control-point producers.
Ran 180 early pipeline configurations and 216 fresh shallow/deep configurations; preserved contention notes and independent output checks.

findings.text: Both original splits reproduced outputs/gradients but neither beat the fastest single-device baseline across nine tested inference settings. Mean digit training was 2.24 s GPU-only versus 2.82 s CPU activations and 3.41 s CPU neurons.
CPU actor/GPU learner PPO averaged 2.96 s versus 3.43 s GPU-only (about 14% less); all 15 finite-task policies reached 100% evaluation success. This is a small synchronous RL workload.

For the idle four-layer producer with 8192 independent curves, full GPU took 1.472 ms, full-batch hybrid 1.877 ms, and best concurrent hybrid 4.030 ms. The dependent tree was 2.385, 3.066, and 15.141 ms respectively. No hybrid beat the fastest baseline in the tested grid.

Fresh one-/four-layer comparisons passed ordered output checks across 216 configurations; 70 related regression checks were reported passed. Deep producer timings use random weights rather than learned predictive performance.

limitations: One eager FP32 desktop implementation; transfer dependencies, scheduling, and untrained stress cases limit generalization.
Original mixed-device inference is single-request/single-stream and not thread-safe; early pipeline pilots ran with competing GPU work.
CPU actor/GPU learner is synchronous PPO, not a distributed or language-model RL result.
projects.status: Completed execution, training, RL, and deeper-producer pipeline studies.
next_steps: Recommendation: Focus further optimization on transfer amortization or independent workloads; benchmark any kernel/pipeline change under matched uncontended conditions.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Layers
projects.purpose: Test content-associated layer selection across CPU/GPU boundaries, then reverse the split to keep the expert bank in system RAM.
work: Implemented CPU-selected layers/GPU experts and GPU-selected layers/CPU experts, catalogues, grouped dispatch, cached geometry, pinned transfers, and decision-cadence controls.
Completed six original digit checkpoints, cached/uncached timing studies, a trained 50.9M-parameter EMNIST model, and an untrained 269.9M execution stress model.

findings.text: Original digit feedback switched layers on 6.20% of predictions and improved assigned-family selection from 91.48% to 95.83%; final accuracy was 95.46% versus 95.56% for separately trained entry-only selection, without a demonstrated overall improvement.
The 50,915,372-parameter model achieved 77.95% on 9400 EMNIST test images, identical across seven execution variants. Layer switching occurred on 28.97%; maximum logit difference was 1.14e-5.
Reversed grouped dispatch beat matching CPU-only execution in 0/12 median settings and the fastest single-device baseline in 0/12. The 269,946,720-parameter stress model was untrained.

At batch 128, reversed placement reduced GPU tensor peaks to about 9.14 MiB for the trained model and 9.16 MiB for the stress model, with expert weights in system RAM. Four decisions transfer 160 logical bytes per input; total model bytes are not compressed.

limitations: Original study has three seeds; larger EMNIST study has one seed and assigned class groups taught with auxiliary labels.
Synchronous device decisions add dependent communication; CPU-only already has zero GPU weight residency.
No LLM, model paging, RL, fused-kernel, or reversed-training-speed result.
projects.status: Completed both split directions; placement and feedback verified, speed advantage unestablished.
next_steps: Recommendation: Treat RAM placement as a deployment tradeoff; compare to CPU-only and optimize larger workloads before claiming speed gains.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Steer
projects.purpose: Measure whether curve-guided internal computation produces more distinct correct Boolean programs for a complete request budget.
work: Trained five architectures across three seeds on disjoint truth-table functions; evaluated 2/4/8 internal steps, latent/route interventions, candidate sampling, verification, and structural deduplication.
Built an exhaustive 16-input correctness verifier, saved generated programs and routes, and exported verified Python alternatives.

findings.text: At 64 attempts per task, Bezier solved 85.29% with 3.217 distinct correct programs/task, 5.81 ms complete request time, and 1.278 MiB checkpoint. Fixed routing solved 86.91%, yielded 3.473 alternatives, and took 4.91 ms at 1.243 MiB.

Only 7.63% of raw Bezier candidates were correct. The 85.29% task solve rate is success in up to 64 attempts, not single-attempt accuracy; the difference from fixed routing was -1.63 percentage points with exploratory 95% interval [-4.36,+1.04].

With hidden state fixed and deterministic decoding, 64 curves solved 14.71% versus 10.55% for one route, but only 0.52% of tasks produced two or more distinct correct structures from curve changes alone. Most variety came from token sampling.
Bezier 2/4/8 updates produced 85.03%/85.29%/85.09% solve rates while request time increased 4.92/5.81/7.11 ms. No efficiency, correctness, or storage advantage was demonstrated.

limitations: Finite four-input Boolean program synthesis; grammar enforces syntax and exhaustive verification applies only to this domain.
Three seeds, 512 held-out functions, and post-training curve-only interventions do not establish general coding or reasoning performance.
Same candidate count is not identical compute cost; timings include failures, verification, and deduplication but exclude startup/loading.
projects.status: Completed generative steering study; small steering effect, no overall advantage.
next_steps: Recommendation: Evaluate explicit curve-only training objectives and retain verifier-aware full request cost as the comparison unit.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Think
projects.purpose: Test whether extra shared latent model passes help a small coding agent approach a larger pretrained model.
work: Compared Bezier, straight, and ordinary recurrence at 2/4/8/16/32 internal steps across two seeds, plus trained zero-step and unmodified 1.5B/14B controls.
Completed 34 conditions, each on 12 MBPP functions and four three-stage authored projects, with adapter fitting, tool traces, latency probes, and saved audits.

findings.text: Recurrent 1.5B variants passed 9-10 of 24 stages, compared with 9 for trained zero-step controls and 20 for the 14B model. Small models completed 0/4 projects; 14B completed 2/4.

No consistent quality rise occurred from 2 to 32 steps, and every paired 95% interval for Bezier versus ordinary recurrence included zero. The unmodified small control passed only 1/24, so protocol training is a major separate factor.

At 32 steps Bezier averaged about 1.35 seconds for a common 32-token probe versus 1.15 seconds for the 14B control; batch-one peak CUDA allocations were about 2.92 and 27.65 GiB. Straight and ordinary recurrence had almost the same small footprint.

The added recurrence is an adapter around the full pretrained transformer; each internal step adds a complete shared causal-LM pass and KV-cache position. It does not replace or compress the base stack.

limitations: Small restricted-Python benchmark, two fitting seeds, 16 task families; public-task pretraining overlap unknown.
Training teaches JSON tool protocol as well as code; executor restrictions can reject otherwise ordinary Python.
Lower memory primarily reflects 1.5B versus 14B weights; added latent work still costs time and cache entries.
projects.status: Completed 34-condition coding pilot; extra steps did not close the quality gap.
next_steps: Recommendation: Improve protocol/code training and use matched compute/parameter controls before increasing latent depth.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-Revisit
projects.purpose: Isolate routing and leave-and-return visits in a shared recurrent coding model under matched stored parameters and matrix-computation budgets.
work: Fitted Bezier, non-geometric routing, and ordinary recurrence on a frozen Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B base; tested 4/8/16 passes and no-return interventions.
Audited 864 stage trials and 3335 actions, six adapters, source/data hashes, arithmetic budgets, revisit traces, and standalone/batched generation behavior.

findings.text: At the prespecified eight-pass budget, Bezier passed 28/72 stages, ordinary recurrence 30/72, and non-geometric routing 28/72; all completed 0/8 projects. Each primary arm had 1,545,352,240 total and 1,637,936 trainable parameters.

Allowing Bezier returns improved stage success by 1.39 percentage points versus a post-training blocked-return intervention, with paired interval [0,+4.69]. This is not a retrained ablation and does not isolate geometry from changed route distributions.
All 277 eight-pass Bezier actions had leave-and-return events; blocking eliminated those events. Frequent revisits are measurable but did not establish more useful reasoning.

One standalone demo failed although its original batch-of-four evaluation passed. Diagnostic replay reproduced the batch's first actions; serial generation repeated a different first action. The saved BF16 benchmark is batch-sensitive.

limitations: Two seeds, 24 fresh MBPP functions and four reused projects; no general coding-agent or compression claim.
Only 190 detailed update records remain although final metadata reports 192 updates; final two individual loss/gradient records were not saved.
Dense field execution matches arithmetic but is not a sparse-dispatch speedup; timing probes were noisy.
projects.status: Completed matched recurrence study and audit; no clear Bezier coding benefit.
next_steps: Recommendation: Investigate batch-sensitive generation and preserve exact evaluation configuration; expand task families and independent seeds.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-LongHorizon
projects.purpose: Build compressed GPT-OSS-120B artifacts and test a distilled shared-field replacement plus controller RL on bounded coding and cumulative workflows.
work: Requantized expert weights into a three-bit Bezier codebook; built SSD-streamed execution with packed expert caching and a verified decoder.
Replaced one expert bank using supervised distillation; ran eight controller-only REINFORCE episodes and exported standalone distilled/RL variants.
Evaluated four authored coding tasks and one six-stage cumulative project; retained output/token IDs, hidden checks, timing, source/export hashes, and mechanism controls.

findings.text: Logical standalone deployment sizes were 60.794 GiB native MXFP4, 47.453 GiB Bezier three-bit, and 46.256 GiB compact variants: 21.945% and 23.913% smaller than native. Shared hardlinks mean these are not incremental physical disk totals.

By four attempts, native and three-bit models solved 3/4 coding tasks, distilled compact 4/4, and compact+RL 3/4. The lone distinguishing task depended on finishing under a 384-token limit, so the compact win does not establish stronger general reasoning.

Native, three-bit, and pre-RL compact passed cumulative stages 1-5 and finished with 10/12 checks; RL passed only stage 1 and finished with 8/12. No variant passed the final stage. RL introduced absent-item edge-case failures.

RL changed only 16,841 controller parameters across eight episodes; it did not compress weights or train the full base. Curved, straight, and frozen local reconstruction MSEs were similar (~0.0902), without matched coding evaluations for every geometry control.

limitations: Four tiny authored tasks, one dependent workflow, one fitting/RL seed, low reasoning effort, and tight output caps.
Later variants used a different verified packed-cache runtime, so descriptive request times do not isolate an architectural speedup.
Artifacts do not fit entirely in 32 GiB VRAM; SSD streaming and shared desktop variability matter.
One expert-bank replacement, short-context prompts (max prompt+output 2681 tokens), and eight RL episodes are not general long-horizon evidence.
projects.status: Completed compression and bounded coding pilot; controller RL regressed measured outcomes.
next_steps: Recommendation: Keep pre-RL compact control; broaden independent workflows with matched runtime, reasoning budgets, seeds, and geometry controls.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-MemorySphere
projects.purpose: Train a full-stack spatial recurrent token model from scratch using clustered context keys, fixed scratch slots, Bezier routing, and learned surface output.
work: Implemented a 1,538,295-parameter custom model with 16 addressed regions, 256-dimensional state, 64-dimensional keys, and four overwritten scratch KV slots.
Completed 44 conditions and 2640 stage-runs across route/depth/halting settings plus independent pretrained capability references; saved models, tokenizer, traces, memory probes, and regrading.

findings.text: Adaptive Bezier and straight routing each passed 6/120 stage-runs across two seeds; direct routing passed 7/120. The independent 14B reference passed 48/60.
No sphere condition solved long-chain or MBPP transfer tasks or a complete project. Bounded internal scratch memory did not translate into a coding-quality advantage.
All three routing controls kept single-row tensor allocation flat through 128 internal steps. This result concerns fixed internal scratch state, not unbounded text-context or training memory.
Independent regrading of 1400 unique code/check pairs found zero score discrepancies, and wider-batch replay produced identical outputs.

limitations: Small from-scratch model and narrow restricted agent task domain, not a general coding assistant.
All 16 regions were evaluated densely before mixing, so this study does not measure optimized sparse dispatch.
Surface contact is an output address, not correctness; pretrained references are independent capability baselines, not matched architectures.
projects.status: Completed from-scratch prototype; bounded memory verified, coding quality low.
next_steps: Recommendation: Use this model as an auditable mechanism baseline; improve training/data and maintain non-geometric controls during scaling.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-MemorySphere-7B
projects.purpose: Scale the from-scratch sphere architecture to 7.35B independent parameters and validate training, sparse dispatch, checkpointing, and bounded-depth inference.
work: Built 64 spatial regions with large independent matrices, a 4096-state recurrent core, selected-region sparse execution, own 2048-token BPE, and factored Adafactor gradient-release updates.
Completed a 600-update local pilot from random initialization, six task evaluation depth/stopping conditions, depth/memory timing, independent regrading, and save/resume checks.

findings.text: The model has 7,346,916,807 independent parameters; the pilot supervised 14,612 sampled answer tokens and took about 8.6 minutes including validation/saving. This is a feasibility run, not full pretraining.
Every 2/4/8/16/32-visit and adaptive condition passed 0/60 task stages, often emitting finish before a useful edit. Better held-out token prediction did not yield completed programs.

Observed peak training allocation was 20.02 GiB and batch-one inference 13.72 GiB. A 32-token continuation took 0.277 s at two visits and 3.044 s at 32; fixed-workload allocation stayed level through 128 visits.

All 7.35B weights remain resident; four selected matrices contain 440,664,064 parameters, with a conservative per-visit accessible total of 736,955,847 including shared parameters. Sparse dispatch saves matrix work, not resident weight storage.

limitations: One seed/recipe with only 600 updates and no freshly trained 7B straight or ordinary controls.
Tiny supervised-token budget relative to model size; clustering does not physically compress text KV cache.
No full FP32 optimizer master copy, BF16 rounding limits, and narrow corpus; context and training memory still grow.
projects.status: Completed 7.35B feasibility pilot; 0/60 at every evaluated depth.
next_steps: Recommendation: Use the later 7.41B full-target training run for the next evidence point; retain this pilot as feasibility evidence.
projects.date_note: Saved local evidence reviewed for the 2026-11-25 consolidation; historical tests and measurements were not rerun.

projects.name: Bezier-MemorySphere-7B-Training
projects.purpose: Run a substantial time-bounded local training experiment from scratch with fuller token supervision and a broader coding/action corpus.
work: Built a 7,405,637,063-parameter variant with an own 16K tokenizer, full sampled code-window and action-token targets, staged code/agent mixing, and stochastic BF16 Adafactor updates.
Prepared 32000 Python files (42.6M stored training tokens), 6575 coding tasks, and 48118 supervised actions; froze validation/test panels and retained provenance/filtering records.
Completed the ten-hour run and a later read-only checkpoint/generation diagnostic; retained completion, token losses, partial task panels, model shards, optimizer/RNG state, and traces.

findings.text: Training completed on 2026-11-24 at 11:52:48 UTC (06:52:48 America/New_York), after 22,042 updates and 4,774,503 supervised tokens. The best/evaluated checkpoint was u0022042. This supersedes the README/handoff's live or underway description.

Final evaluation timed out before both 96-task panels finished: eight visits scored 0/60 and adaptive scored 0/40, with zero passing code or finished workflows. These are incomplete panels, not 0/96 results.

Validation code NLL improved from 9.7171 to 5.9733 and agent NLL from 9.7395 to 2.4168; agent token accuracy reached 47.20%. However, all 180 recorded eight-visit actions and all 116 adaptive actions were invalid, with no successful edits.

The later check-in verified all 27 checkpoint-file SHA-256 checks and frozen source matches. Full-context decoding on two validation prompts also generated malformed repetitive output; it differed from cached decoding. No training was restarted by the check-in.
The run recorded 30.097 GiB peak allocated tensors, 7696 distinct code records and 9960 distinct agent records. Stored corpus tokens are not equivalent to the 4.77M actually supervised tokens.

limitations: Training-budget completion does not establish working agentic coding; held-out scoring was partial and yielded no successes.
Single model/run, limited training exposure, no matched from-scratch geometry controls, and incomplete semantic decontamination.
Cached versus full-context outputs differ; diagnostic malformed output in both paths does not identify a single failure cause.
Historical status keep_awake/pid fields are saved metadata, not proof a worker is still running.
projects.status: Training completed; final task panels incomplete; no working coding-agent capability demonstrated.
next_steps: Recommendation: Prioritize valid tool generation and cached/full-context consistency diagnostics, then complete fixed held-out panels before any longer training claim.
Recommendation: Update project-facing status prose to the completion/check-in evidence while preserving original records.

projects.name: Nested core v1 - shared checker prototype
projects.purpose: Test whether a tiny direct-path view of the outer model's own core weights can predict useful mid-route changes on Python next-byte prediction.
work: Built a causal byte encoder, cubic sphere routes, nearest-two expert visits, fixed-exit tail redirection, and a 64-to-16-to-1 checker drawn from outer-expert tensor views.
Implemented immediate serial, delayed single-stream reference, and concurrent CUDA-stream checking, including fixed-shape CUDA Graph inference.
Completed a six-arm, seed-7 integration experiment with 24 updates per arm and a 64-prefix evaluation cap per split.
Preserved reproducible corpus and source identities, resumable checkpoints, shared-weight audits, paired file-bootstrap evaluation, trajectory plots, and profiler/resource measurements.
Preserved a separate untrained overlap probe and an earlier smoke run that failed its initial audit.

findings.text: Shared arms contain 191,372 learned parameters and add zero checker parameters; the private checker adds 1,057. Sharing is a storage result, not zero computational cost.

At 16 visits, concurrent full-turn test NLL was 4.101342 nats per byte versus clean-outer 4.084265. Full versus zero-turn gain was 0.012108 with 95% paired interval [-0.010313, 0.034523]; full versus clean gain was -0.017078 [-0.046866, 0.015950]. Useful accuracy improvement was not established.
The concurrent model averaged 2.844 redirects, but full versus one-turn NLL gain was -0.001781 [-0.019655, 0.018584]. Redirect activity did not establish a repeated-steering benefit.

Profiler evidence observed eager and captured-graph kernel overlap; the no-checker graph did not overlap. Batch-one captured concurrent inference was 1.285 ms versus 1.509 ms for the same-policy pipeline reference, but clean graph inference was 0.660 ms. Eager concurrent inference was slower than the reference (21.172 versus 19.227 ms).
The suite records complete execution, pilot_only scientific status, a failed sample criterion, and an incomplete full protocol.

limitations: One seed, 24 updates, and only 64 prefixes per split; the five-seed full protocol was not executed.
Python next-byte scores are not directly comparable with the Boolean answer tasks introduced in v2.
Training labels use detached snapshot activations; v2 later introduced live control gradients into the outer representation.
A region is a computational address, and the inner-sphere radius is not a hard gate on core-expert execution.
Saved benchmark results are hardware- and execution-mode-specific; this index did not rerun them.
projects.status: Completed integration pilot; no demonstrated quality benefit; retained as the original shared-slice prototype.
next_steps: Recommendation: use the later whole-core revisions for new work; retain v1 as the Python next-byte and concurrency reference.
Recommendation: if revisiting its hypothesis, run the preregistered uncapped multi-seed matrix before making quality claims.
projects.date_note: Indexed saved artifacts on November 25, 2026. README identifies v2 as the revision requested November 24; no live training status was inferred.

projects.name: Nested core v2 - fixed whole-core budget
projects.purpose: Constrain the entire central region to 1,312 shared parameters and jointly train direct Boolean reasoning, initial routing, outer computation, and live redirection control.
work: Replaced v1's shared tensor slice with a complete 64-to-16-to-16 core, fixed at the origin, with all four parameter tensors shared across roles.
Added parameter-free syntax features, independently verified Boolean programs, and program/truth-table-disjoint train, validation, test, and longer-program splits.
Added gain regression and ranking supervision whose gradients reach the live outer representation, plus a detached-control ablation.
Completed a seven-arm, seed-7, 128-update pilot with 128 examples (eight complete program truth tables) evaluated per split.
Recorded gradient interaction, routing coverage, core participation, counterfactual regret, CUDA overlap, latency, memory, and separate CPU learning diagnostics.

findings.text: The entire core contains exactly 1,312 learned parameters. Shared models contain 175,328 parameters; the private-core control contains 176,640. Whole-core identity, tensor participation, and control gradients into the encoder passed the saved audit.

All seven pilot arms achieved 50.00% outer answer accuracy at 16 visits. The primary concurrent core reached 50.78% direct-core accuracy and 46.88% on longer programs; its outer NLL was 0.704778 versus clean 0.703922.
The primary concurrent arm accepted no redirects at its validation-selected margin. Full, one-turn, and zero-turn predictions were identical; the combined reasoning/control/routing criterion failed.

A one-batch gradient audit found direct-reasoning versus control cosine -0.095453 and outer-answer versus control cosine -0.030264. These local conflicts are diagnostic, not established causes of the poor scores.

Captured concurrent batch-one inference took 1.511 ms versus the same-policy reference's 1.842 ms, while clean inference took 0.965 ms. Eager and graph kernel overlap were observed, but the full controlled model was not faster than the clean baseline.

A separate raw-input CPU probe at learning rate 0.003 selected step 1,000 with validation NLL 0.676549 and 54.10% accuracy; its final step 5,000 NLL worsened to 1.079140. These training/validation diagnostics did not evaluate test or OOD examples.

limitations: The completed run is a short, capped, one-seed pilot; full seven-arm, five-seed confirmation remains unexecuted.
Computation concentrated on a small subset of regions; broad routing diversity was not demonstrated.
Controller regret is audited at the first eligible decision, not every later checkpoint.
Sharing all weights does not ensure that reasoning and control objectives are compatible.
Outer and core results concern a constrained Boolean benchmark, not general language or logical reasoning.
projects.status: Completed seven-arm feasibility pilot; integrity checks passed but the quality criterion failed.
next_steps: Recommendation: retain v2 as the fixed 1,312-parameter baseline against the larger-core revisions.
Recommendation: investigate the direct-core learning bottleneck and routing concentration before promoting a full study; v3 and v4 provide saved follow-ups.
projects.date_note: Saved results inspected November 25, 2026. Scientific status remains pilot_only in suite.json.

projects.name: Nested core v3 - scaling a 5% shared core
projects.purpose: Test larger outer models with a proportionally larger shared core, more training data, staged warmup, and validation-selected joint checkpoints.
work: Built small (183,239 total / 9,223 core parameters) and large (4,704,970 total / 235,210 core parameters) models, keeping the complete shared core near 5% of the model.
Expanded training to 1,024 Boolean programs, 256 distinct functions, and 16,384 examples while preserving the original 512-example validation, test, and longer-program splits.
Completed all seven planned arm/seed runs: small clean/shared seed 7; large clean/shared seeds 7 and 19; large private-core seed 7.
Used 500 core-only, 256 outer-warmup, and 1,500 joint updates per run; recorded best and final checkpoints, full heldout evaluations, paired-program comparisons, and source/data verification.
Ran CPU direct-core learning probes and a training-only input-memory diagnostic that motivated revision 4.

findings.text: All 7/7 runs completed all 2,256 updates, with complete 512-example heldout evaluations and validation-selected joint checkpoints. The bounded study's combined quality outcome failed across its shared runs despite passing whole-core sharing and geometry integrity checks.

Large shared seed 7 reached 53.52% outer accuracy and 0.6705 answer NLL versus clean 50.00% and 0.6948. Seed 19 reached 51.76% and 0.6931 versus clean 50.00% and 0.6938. Small clean and shared models both remained at 50.00% outer accuracy.

Large shared seed 7 made zero redirects, so its better clean-control score cannot be attributed to useful repeated steering. Seed 19 averaged 1.980 redirects, but full versus zero-turn gain was 0.000211 with 95% paired interval [-0.000283, 0.000607], and full versus one-turn gain was -0.000012 [-0.000058, 0.000035].

Large shared direct-core accuracy was 58.79% (seed 7) and 59.77% (seed 19), but longer-program core accuracy was 50.00% and 49.02%. The enlarged core learned modest in-distribution structure without reliable longer-program reasoning.

Large seed-7 captured concurrent batch-one inference took 1.811 ms versus the same-policy reference's 2.213 ms, but clean graph inference took 1.296 ms. No-checker graphs also overlapped, so graph overlap alone cannot attribute concurrency to checker work.

Standalone 235,210-parameter core probes selected validation NLL 0.67921 at learning rate 0.003 / step 500 and 0.68337 at 0.001 / step 1,500. Both final 2,000-update NLLs worsened, motivating bounded warmup with validation selection.

A training-only diagnostic over 48 programs and all 16 input assignments found strong attenuation of input-bit perturbations by the recurrent outer encoder and traversal. This identified a representation bottleneck and motivated v4's parameter-free syntax/input skip.

limitations: Only two large-model seeds and one small-model seed; no cross-seed confidence estimate.
The larger original seven-arm protocol was not executed; the private control was only run for large seed 7.
The reused benchmark holdouts are not a new sequestered confirmation set.
v2-to-v3 differences include capacity, core fraction, data, training duration, optimization, and selection; their results do not isolate scaling alone.
Program-bootstrap intervals describe program uncertainty within a seed, not training-seed variation.
projects.status: Completed seven-run bounded scale-up; modest reasoning gains, but repeated-steering and combined quality criteria failed.
next_steps: Recommendation: preserve v3 as the matched reference for v4's representation intervention.
Recommendation: replicate the larger model across more seeds and separate input preservation, core capacity, and control supervision in future ablations.

projects.name: Nested core v4 - preserve input information
projects.purpose: Test whether a parameter-free syntax/input skip fixes the outer representation bottleneck while preserving v3's 5% shared core, parameter count, corpus, and training recipe.
work: Added a fixed syntax/input skip to the recurrent encoder output in both clean and shared-controller arms, using existing deterministic projection buffers and no answer execution.
Retained 4,704,970 total parameters and a fully shared 235,210-parameter core; completed the matched seed-7 clean/shared pair with 2,256 updates each.
Evaluated complete held-out splits of 512 answer-prefix cases from 32 program files, saved validation-selected best and full-endpoint checkpoints, and compared matched v3/v4 results and provenance.
Recorded artifact verification, shared-role gradient audits, CUDA timing/overlap, trajectory data, and an offline interactive experiment visualization.

findings.text: On 512 held-out answer-prefix cases from 32 program files in seed 7, the same shared checkpoint improved from 52.73% with redirects disabled to 57.62% with redirects enabled, averaging 6.055 redirects per 16 visits. Answer NLL fell from 0.657042 to 0.646470. The separately trained clean model reached 57.03% accuracy; the 4.89-point increase is versus disabled redirects, not versus that clean model.

Full-turn NLL gain was 0.010572 [95% paired-program interval 0.008350, 0.012941] versus zero turns; 0.004572 [0.003005, 0.006242] versus one turn; and 0.011479 [0.001261, 0.021992] versus the separately trained clean control. The saved per-seed combined criterion passed.

Against the matched v3 seed-7 run, v4 reduced full-turn NLL by 0.024027 [0.016075, 0.032539] for the shared arm and 0.036815 [0.024529, 0.048552] for the clean arm. Both arms benefited from the input representation change.

Shared direct-core accuracy was 59.57%, but longer-program core accuracy was 49.80%. Clean direct-core accuracy was 62.50%. Useful steering in this seed did not establish robust longer-program reasoning.

The saved verification confirms two completed runs, identical v3 corpus, validation-only checkpoint selection, exact source snapshots, whole-core participation, and the selected shared update 1,756. The full original protocol remains unexecuted; suite scientific status is pilot_only.

Captured concurrent batch-one latency was 1.894 ms versus 2.297 ms for the same-checkpoint pipeline reference and 1.377 ms for clean inference. The shared model therefore retained a runtime cost versus the clean baseline, despite scheduling savings within the controlled model.

limitations: One seed and an adaptive follow-up using reused holdouts. The 512 answer-prefix cases are grouped within 32 programs; program-bootstrap intervals do not establish replication across training seeds.
Multiple descriptive intervals were reported without a multiplicity-adjusted study-level success gate.
Validation-selected checkpoints and margins differ between revisions and arms.
Longer-program reasoning remains approximately chance, and the shared direct core does not outperform the clean direct core.
The no-checker graph also contains kernel overlap; eager named-scope profiling is needed for checker/outer attribution.
projects.status: Completed two-arm exploratory follow-up; first positive per-seed steering criterion in this family, awaiting independent replication.
next_steps: Recommendation: replicate the clean/shared input-preserving comparison with additional seeds and a new sequestered program holdout.
Recommendation: add ablations that isolate input bits, syntax structure, and control supervision, and evaluate control competence at later redirect checkpoints.
Recommendation: retain the latency and longer-program limitations alongside any positive steering claim.

projects.name: Pretrained 7B shared-core pilot
projects.purpose: Test whether a central core sharing 15% of a pretrained Mistral model can reason independently and choose useful inference-time MLP substitutions.
work: Adapted Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 on bounded Python patch review using matched baseline and shared-controller arms.
Implemented a logical central core with actual parameter aliases, single Bézier-endpoint MLP substitution, independent-core inference, held-out paired evaluation, and CUDA graph concurrency checks.
Completed 512 joint updates per arm; saved frozen protocols, checkpoints, corpus identities and evaluation records.

findings.text: The full model has 7,248,023,552 parameters; 1,087,201,280 (14.9999689184%) belong to the shared core, with zero added learned parameters. This is full-weight adaptation of a pretrained 7B model, not training a 7B model from scratch.

On 128 swapped presentations per split, the trained baseline and shared model both reached 100% test accuracy and 99.22% longer-chain OOD accuracy; the independently executed core stayed at 50% on both. The balanced task is bounded contract consistency, not general code repair.

Validation selected a threshold above the bounded controller score range, producing no turns and exactly zero same-checkpoint steering gain. The intended reasoning-and-control capability was not achieved.
The report records 44 passing tests and finite nonzero gradients in every core parameter tensor for each audited objective; this establishes implementation participation rather than useful reasoning.

A later CUDA-graph check observed 72.21875 microseconds of cross-stream kernel overlap over four profiled checker/lookahead calls. Four timing samples gave serial/parallel medians 37.16/37.02 ms, insufficient to establish speedup.

limitations: One training seed and a narrow task with an outer-model accuracy ceiling.
One endpoint-addressed MLP substitution; original attention/suffix order remains, with no arbitrary repeated traversal.
Core position is a logical address, not physical GPU placement; shared weights still have compute and storage costs.
projects.status: Completed pilot; adaptation succeeds on its bounded task, independent core reasoning and useful rerouting not demonstrated.
next_steps: Recommended: prioritize core capability and harder continuation decisions before more routing complexity; follow-up distillation is implemented in v2.
Recommended: compare joint training with a matched outer-only training arm and use fresh held-out programs across multiple seeds.

projects.name: Shared-core distillation and scaffolded reasoning
projects.purpose: Improve the shared core through dense intermediate supervision, recurrence and teacher distillation while retaining the earlier patch-review ability.
work: Added verified multi-stage arithmetic programs, training-only teacher caches, gold intermediate-state supervision and four tied core passes.
Ran a guarded main attempt and validation-guided recovery; selected recovery checkpoint best_u000512.
Evaluated direct answers, fixed-format free-running traces, fixed-action/permuted routing controls, core restoration and recurrence.

findings.text: The main run stopped at update 384 after retention-guard failure; recovery completed 768 updates, with its local update 512 selected. The 1,152 attempted updates do not equal retained weight-lineage updates.

On the fixed 16-program/64-example scaffolded test panel, outer state accuracy rose from 18.18% to 95.45%, final answer from 51.56% to 95.31%, and whole-trace correctness reached 90.63%. The core achieved 10.91% state, 53.13% final and 0% whole-trace accuracy.

Full direct-answer test accuracy was 53.71% with control disabled, 53.32% with steering and 50.98% for the core across 512 examples. The 95% scaffolded-panel result is not a full direct-answer result.

Deployed steering reduced same-checkpoint full NLL by 0.045572 nats, but accuracy changed -0.391 percentage points with an interval crossing zero. The learned controller did not beat the same-candidate always-turn control; permutation p=0.249 provided no support for input-specific alignment.

Restoring the pre-v2 core improved direct-answer NLL on test/OOD; four core passes had worse NLL than one. These diagnostics do not attribute the scaffolded outer improvement to independent core reasoning.

limitations: Single seed, adaptive recovery and bundled training changes; no causal isolation of distillation, recurrence or controller training.
Trace outputs are constrained digits/A/B with a supplied format, not unrestricted text generation or compute-matched direct answers.
Only one delayed MLP substitution; cached counterfactual and deployed metrics differ numerically and must be kept separate.
projects.status: Completed; strong outer scaffolded-trace learning, but independent core reasoning and useful conditional control not established.
next_steps: Recommended: retain the scaffolded-trace result with its exact 64-example scope.
Recommended: separate reasoning quality, weight adaptation and inference-time controller gain in future experiments; v3 pursues controller evaluation and streaming.

projects.name: Shared-core control with streamed GPU residency
projects.purpose: Test useful conditional control and lower GPU residency while retaining the complete pretrained model.
work: Relocated the logical shared core to layers 17-21 without adding learned weights.
Completed guarded recovery training and fresh held-out program evaluation.
Built synchronous CPU-backed outer-weight streaming with a persistent core and bounded block cache; measured exact output parity, allocation and latency.

findings.text: Recovery completed 512 updates after the earlier main attempt failed a retention guard at update 128. Validation selected Always Stay, so conditional control contributed zero accuracy/NLL gain.

Fresh 512-example test accuracy improved from 53.52% to 63.67% with control disabled (+10.16 percentage points, paired 95% interval +5.66 to +14.65); OOD rose 53.71% to 58.59%. These are weight-adaptation gains, with no matched outer-only-training ablation.

Streaming reduced measured peak CUDA allocation from 13.5974 to 3.4421 GiB (74.69%) for four 139-token prompts, while controlled-forward median increased from 79.661 to 1,208.119 ms (15.17x) and an eight-token generation probe became 29.16x slower.
Four resident/streamed routing cases matched logits, tokens and decisions bitwise; all eight generation tokens matched. The report records 42/42 CPU tests.
Core-restoration accuracy and NLL intervals all included zero; fixed-panel whole-trace correctness declined from 60/64 to 58/64. The arithmetic generation smoke executed but answered incorrectly.

limitations: Streaming is a general offloading mechanism, retains full CPU-backed model storage, and does not show a geometry-specific advantage.
Synchronous single request; no KV cache or prefetch; every generated token recomputes context.
One seed, fixed location and candidate pair; short runtime samples and desktop load limit timing generalization.
projects.status: Completed; lower GPU allocation and exact streamed parity demonstrated, with large latency costs; conditional control not useful.
next_steps: Recommended: treat low-residency streaming as a memory/latency tradeoff, not an inference-speed improvement.
Recommended: evaluate resident shared execution separately; that is the v4 branch.

projects.name: Resident shared-core controller
projects.purpose: Test whether a separate execution context using the same resident core storage can choose beneficial outer-layer substitutions.
work: Optimized exact core slices while freezing the other 85% of the 7B model.
Probed route candidates on training data; compared MLP 27/29 substitutions at application layer 28.
Completed training, selected an active candidate under a disclosed validation-rule amendment, and ran fresh test/OOD, shuffled controls, weight audits and resident runtime checks.

findings.text: Training completed 1,365 total updates (1,024 reasoning plus 341 replay); the selected checkpoint retained 768 reasoning/256 replay updates. All 6,160,822,272 outside-core elements remained bitwise unchanged; all 48 core-bearing tensors changed.
The original selector chose Always Stay. A secondary rule adopted after validation inspection selected the active update-768 candidate; this amendment must accompany the result.

On 1,024 fresh test examples, learned routing scored 66.6992% versus 65.8203% disabled (+0.879 percentage points, 95% interval -0.879 to +2.637) and 67.0898% shuffled. OOD learned accuracy was 57.7148% versus 58.0078% disabled.
The controller made active decisions but never selected MLP 27 on test/OOD. Test rescues/spoils were 55/46 with strong answer-position asymmetry; this does not establish semantic routing benefit.

Creating a core execution view allocated zero additional CUDA bytes. On four 141-token prompts, controlled inference took 90.377 ms versus 70.724 ms disabled (1.278x), with no observed simultaneous GPU-kernel overlap.
All five final tasks completed and 49 CPU tests passed; the generation smoke ran but returned the wrong arithmetic answer.

limitations: One seed, one substitution, fixed geometry and a selection amendment.
No matched outer-only-training ablation; exact storage and preservation do not imply useful control.
No offloading, quantization or KV cache; short runtime samples are not a serving benchmark.
projects.status: Completed; exact shared residency and update scope verified, useful conditional control not demonstrated.
next_steps: Recommended: compare candidate-relative scores and fixed-denominator tie weighting under a predeclared protocol; v5 implements these follow-ups.
Recommended: require fresh holdouts for further checkpoint or policy selection.

projects.name: Absolute versus relative shared-core scoring
projects.purpose: Test corrected tie weighting and a genuine Stay-reference subtraction in two frozen controller arms.
work: Implemented fixed-denominator control loss and FP32 shared-head margins in both arms.
Compared absolute candidate margins against relative candidate-minus-Stay margins using the same warm start and planned example order.
Preregistered selection, evaluated both frozen arms, preserved the primary arm, and audited selected versus completed training exposure.

findings.text: Absolute completed 1,024 reasoning/341 replay updates and selected update 768; relative stopped at 256/85 after a retention guard and selected update 128 with Always Stay. Completed budgets and controller compute were unequal.

Primary absolute learned test accuracy was 64.7461% versus 65.0391% disabled; OOD was 59.3750% versus 60.1563%. Learned-minus-disabled differences were -0.293 and -0.781 percentage points, with both paired intervals crossing zero.

Relative chose Stay for every test/OOD/replay example: learned, disabled, fixed and shuffled results were identical (65.1367% test, 61.0352% OOD). The higher OOD point estimate cannot be attributed to conditional routing.

Corrected all-tie loss scaling matched approximately 0.08, but first-128-update rescue/spoil AUC remained near chance: 0.489 absolute and 0.515 relative. These are changing-weight training diagnostics.

Both weight audits preserved every outside-core element; extra core-view CUDA allocation was zero. Controlled/disabled median latency was 1.305x absolute and 1.460x relative, without observed kernel overlap.
The report records 68 CPU checks and eight completed final tasks; the free-form generation smoke answered incorrectly.

limitations: Single seed and narrow program task; relative's early guard stop prevents a matched completed-budget comparison.
Both arms share normalization and readout-precision changes, so the arm comparison does not isolate all changes from v4.
Neither arm establishes useful learned steering; relative's failed pilot is not a general disproof of reference subtraction.
projects.status: Completed two-arm pilot; absolute remains frozen primary, neither arm demonstrates conditional benefit.
next_steps: Recommended: preserve the registered primary and report actual exposure rather than describing completed arms as matched.
Recommended: move beyond one whole-MLP substitution only with direct execution audits and strong fixed/shuffled controls; v6 implements node-level routing.
