projects.name: Node-level spatial routing
projects.purpose: Make Bézier coordinates select actual hidden computational nodes in a shared 7B model and test repeated route redirection.
work: Built an atlas covering 987,136 nodes; 147,185 core nodes own the fixed 15% parameter budget.
Implemented node-budgeted MLP and attention projection gathers, coordinate-sensitive dispatch, two controller checkpoints, and selected-path generation.
Corrected a forward-distance degeneracy before held-out testing, completed the revised pilot, and independently reran all held-out prompts through actual deployed dispatch.

findings.text: Coordinates now demonstrably affect computation: swapping selected/unselected MLP node coordinates changed selected sets and logits by up to 0.125; restoring coordinates restored logits bitwise. Full-density greedy tokens matched dense inference in the audit, with maximum BF16 logit difference 0.0625.

The first sampler produced identical late route node sets; the revised forward window changed all 60 later stage groups after Stay. Revised training produced 255/256 nonzero second-checkpoint targets in its first 64 updates. The failing attempt is retained.

Revised training completed 128 reasoning plus 32 replay updates. Actual deployed test accuracy was 66.4063% learned, 59.3750% spatial Stay, 66.0156% validation-best fixed and 65.6250% shuffled, across 256 examples.

Learned-minus-Stay test gain was +7.031 percentage points [95% CI +1.172, +12.891], but learned-minus-fixed was only +0.391 [-0.781, +1.953]. OOD learned and fixed both scored 59.3750%; useful input-specific control remains unproven.

All held-out examples took action 2 at the first checkpoint. Learned and fixed predictions differed on only three test examples and none on OOD, so a constant route reproduced most of the measured benefit.

Actual deployed verification supersedes cached-tree metrics: cached/output equality and NLL tolerance checks were false despite matched actions. Learned and shuffled dispatch had some prediction/NLL differences; no policy was reselected.

On two 31-token prompts, dense/Stay/learned median latency was 23.244/97.237/119.918 ms. Full weights remained resident, another core view used zero additional CUDA bytes, and all outside-core elements were preserved. The report records 33 CPU tests.

limitations: Density 0.98 with fixed coordinates; dense causal attention and transformer layer dependencies remain.
Mandatory input/output vocabulary interfaces are scheduled spatially rather than sparsified.
One small pilot, no KV cache, no measured total-VRAM advantage versus a single dense model; transient gathers add overhead.
One temporary applications directory was inaccessible during the index scan; primary reports and result artifacts were readable.
projects.status: Completed revised pilot and deployed verification; geometry causally changes computation, conditional advantage over fixed/shuffled routes unresolved.
next_steps: Recommended: optimize grouping/selection overhead without weakening parity checks; v7 records that work.
Recommended: retain deployed metrics as authoritative and require learned gains over fixed and shuffled paths, not only naive Stay.
projects.date_note: Saved report updated November 25, 2026; deployed verification explicitly supersedes cached-tree measurements.

projects.name: Optimized node routing, recurrence and reinforcement learning
projects.purpose: Improve routing execution and input-specific decisions, then explore arbitrary recurrent node reuse, learned stopping and reward-gated coordinate adaptation.
work: Optimized interval grouping and route-plan caching while sharing the original BF16 weight store.
Completed a supervised stage-ordered controller pilot with constrained shared-head readout fitting; gradient-trained checkpoints were evaluated but not selected.
Built arbitrary recurrent global MLP-node/attention-region execution with continue, redirect, revisit and stop; completed a 64-update pilot.
Implemented policy-gradient routing and stopping with reward-gated successful-path coordinate contraction; completed a 256-update pilot and 256-update continuation.
Added persisted optimizer/RNG state, exact restoration audits, clean runtime benchmarks and independent artifact audits.

findings.text: Warm forced-route execution improved over v6 by 1.48x to 9.37x on tested 2/4-prompt layouts; for four 140-token mixed-route prompts, median fell 1,451.79 to 154.96 ms. V7 dense inference still took 69.41 ms. These supplied-action benchmarks exclude learned decisions.

Validation selected a constrained two-row readout fit on original v6 weights, discarding the 256 reasoning/64 replay gradient-updated candidates. The selected stage policy scored 59.24% test versus 60.42% fixed and 60.81% shuffled; OOD was 64.32% versus 64.58% fixed and 65.36% shuffled.

Stage-ordered learned routing missed its registered accuracy criterion. Its selected runtime was 147.74 ms versus 95.18 ms fixed and 69.63 ms dense on four 140-token prompts; 35 CPU tests passed, while the arithmetic generation smoke answered incorrectly.

The 64-update arbitrary recurrent pilot scored 0/128 test and 0/64 OOD for learned/fixed/shuffled paths, while same-weight dense inference scored 61.72%/62.50%. Every learned prompt exhausted eight turns; explicit backward traversal and revisits worked but useful answer quality did not.

The initial 256-update RL pilot learned a constant continue → continue → stop path and constant B answer: 50% on balanced test/OOD, identical to fixed/shuffled predictions. It moved 115,295 outer node positions through 1,905 eligible sampled paths; 113 tests and 40 independent checks passed.

Latest saved continuation completed 256 further updates (512 total). Learned test/OOD accuracy stayed 50% (64/128 and 32/64), again constant B with the same two-turn path. Same-weight dense scores were 53.90625%/56.25%; parent and continuation holdouts differ, so cross-run changes are unpaired.

The continuation changed 66,118 coordinates since its parent; 130,376 were displaced from the original atlas. Core coordinates and locked interfaces stayed fixed. It recorded 1,656 new successful paths and 4,417 accepted contraction events; 140 tests and 57 independent audit checks passed.

Clean continuation runtime for four 140-token prompts was 143.54 ms learned versus 70.09 ms dense, with peak allocations 13.673 versus 13.654 GiB. Lower parameter-application counts did not yield lower batched latency.

A fresh GPU process passed 18 restoration checks for 48 optimizer slices, 85 moment tensors and saved RNGs, without a training step. The first continuation used a fresh optimizer because the parent saved none; subsequent restoration is now supported.

limitations: The stage-ordered, recurrent and RL paths are distinct workstreams; their scores and compute budgets must not be pooled.
Arbitrary pretrained-node reordering is a substantial representation change; execution correctness does not preserve pretrained quality.
RL exploration and coordinate motion occurred during training, but latest greedy inference remains constant and chance-level.
Recurrent prompts execute serially; dense benchmarks use native batching. Parameter-application proxies are not measured hardware FLOPs.
No KV cache; one narrow task family and small recurrent holdouts.
projects.status: Completed stage pilot, recurrent pilot, RL pilot and continuation to 512 updates; implementation and resume audits pass, useful recurrent reasoning/input-specific control not demonstrated.
next_steps: Recommended: diagnose the recurrent representation/answer collapse before adding training duration or spatial complexity.
Recommended: preserve stage-ordered results separately and require nonconstant, held-out gains versus budget-matched fixed/shuffled controls.
Recommended: use saved optimizer/RNG state for further authorized continuation, with a fresh uninspected holdout.
projects.date_note: Latest project documentation updated November 25, 2026. Latest saved RL continuation is 512 total updates; this is an artifact snapshot, not a live-process claim.

projects.name: Paired action-value fitting in shared core weights
projects.purpose: Fit input-sensitive route utility into existing shared core slices using counterbalanced program pairs and out-of-fold second-stage targets.
work: Fitted six 1,024-element row slices (6,144 scalars) of an existing central MLP down projection with no independent controller weight store.
Collected 27,648 route outcomes from 768 fit programs, refreshed 6,912 after first writeback, and calibrated on 192 separate training programs.
Evaluated the frozen learned candidate against fixed, shuffled, prior-v7 and dense controls on fresh verified programs; retained fixed routing as the released default.
Validated cache/dispatch optimizations and selected-path output parity.

findings.text: The full 7B model and fixed shared-core budget are retained, but the fit changes only 6,144 scalars in one existing tensor. All 6,160,822,272 outside-core scalars stayed bitwise unchanged; GPU storage addresses remained stable.
Validation learned and fixed (2,2) each answered 164/256 correctly. Because the release rule required learned accuracy to exceed fixed and shuffled controls, the application defaults to fixed (2,2).

Learned test accuracy was 490/768 (63.80%) versus 485/768 (63.15%) fixed and 481/768 (62.63%) shuffled. Learned-minus-fixed was +0.65 percentage points [-0.65,+1.95]; learned-minus-shuffled +1.17 [-0.65,+2.99]. Neither met the registered criterion.

On longer programs, learned scored 237/384 (61.72%), fixed 224/384 (58.33%), and shuffled 238/384 (61.98%). Learned-minus-fixed +3.39 points [-0.52,+7.29] still included zero; dense fitted-weight inference scored 61.98%.

The controller used all nine action pairs on test, rescuing 17 and spoiling 12 versus fixed; OOD rescues/spoils were 35/22. Diverse decisions and net rescues did not establish input-specific benefit with current uncertainty.

End-to-end learned/fixed/dense median latency was 151.17/95.50/69.79 ms on four 140-token prompts; learned and dense peak allocation was 13.714/13.625 GiB. Replaying selected actions reproduced logits with zero unchosen continuations.

A matched grouping optimization reduced full-tree median 398.81 to 390.59 ms and learned inference 148.61 to 146.64 ms, with bitwise outputs. A 20-entry cache already held all 14 plans in the tested workload. The report records 12 v8 plus 35 inherited tests.

limitations: Bounded arithmetic task, one fitted candidate, short warm full-context timing without KV cache.
Paired intervals condition on one shuffle assignment; primitive operations and prefixes may overlap across distinct final functions.
The same shared rows affect dense predictions and routing features, requiring refreshed outcomes and preservation checks.
The off-template generation smoke answered incorrectly; unrestricted reasoning is not established.
projects.status: Completed frozen pilot; released default remains fixed (2,2), learned conditional advantage unresolved.
next_steps: Recommended: keep the fixed default and report the learned candidate as experimental.
Recommended: target reliable first-checkpoint action values, where validation oracle headroom is largest, using a new holdout for further selection.
